criteria.given: the ProblemCode enum
criteria.when: its values are listed
criteria.then: a new constant STALE exists, appended last so the existing constants keep their order and ordinals: NULL_REQUEST, MISSING_FIELD, INVALID_VALUE, DUPLICATE, CONFLICTING_REQUEST_ID, STALE (values().length == 6)

criteria.given: the static factory Problem.stale(int inputIndex, String requestId, Instant requestedAt, Duration maxAge)
criteria.when: called with inputIndex 3, requestId "R-7", requestedAt 2026-09-01T08:00:00Z and Duration.ofDays(30)
criteria.then: it returns a Problem with inputIndex 3, requestId "R-7", code STALE, field "requestedAt", relatedRequestId null, escalatedFrom null, escalatedTo null and message exactly "R-7 is stale: requestedAt 2026-09-01T08:00:00Z is more than 30 days old" (the day count is maxAge.toDays(); the message names the request id and never the input index)

criteria.given: a WorkRequestValidator built with the new constructor WorkRequestValidator(Clock clock, Duration maxAge), using Clock.fixed(2026-10-20T08:00:00Z, UTC) and Duration.ofDays(30)
criteria.when: validate is called with one otherwise valid request R-1 requestedAt 2026-09-01T08:00:00Z and one valid request R-2 requestedAt 2026-10-19T08:00:00Z
criteria.then: the StageResult requests contain only IndexedRequest for R-2, and problems contain exactly one Problem with code STALE for R-1 at its input index; i.e. a stale request is reported as a problem AND kept out of the queue

criteria.given: a validator with Clock.fixed(2026-10-20T08:00:00Z, UTC) and Duration.ofDays(30)
criteria.when: validate is called with a request requestedAt exactly 2026-09-20T08:00:00Z (exactly 30 days old) and another requestedAt 2026-09-20T07:59:59Z (one second over)
criteria.then: the exactly-30-days request is accepted with no problem and the one-second-older request is STALE: staleness is strictly older than maxAge, i.e. requestedAt.isBefore(now.minus(maxAge))

criteria.given: a validator with a fixed clock and 30 day max age
criteria.when: validate is called with an otherwise valid request whose requestedAt is in the future relative to the clock
criteria.then: the request is accepted into the StageResult requests with no problem of any code (future dates are not a staleness concern)

criteria.given: a validator with a fixed clock and 30 day max age
criteria.when: validate is called with (a) a null element, (b) a request 90 days old that is also missing equipmentId, and (c) a request 90 days old whose requestedAt was unreadable in the raw input and is therefore reported through invalidFieldsByIndex
criteria.then: (a) yields only NULL_REQUEST, (b) yields only the MISSING_FIELD problem for equipmentId and no STALE problem, (c) yields only the INVALID_VALUE problem for requestedAt and no STALE problem: field checks run first and a request that already has field problems is never additionally checked for staleness, so a STALE problem always carries a non-null requestId

criteria.given: a validator with Clock.fixed(2026-10-20T08:00:00Z, UTC) and Duration.ofDays(30)
criteria.when: validate is called with 3 requests of which R-7 is 90 days old and R-3 is missing description
criteria.then: the returned StageTrace has stage "validate", in 3, out 1, and notes exactly ["R-3 rejected: missing description", "R-7 rejected: stale"] — one note per rejected request, stale notes read "<requestId> rejected: stale", notes stay sorted naturally and contain no input index

criteria.given: a validator built with the preserved no-argument constructor new WorkRequestValidator()
criteria.when: validate is called with requests dated years in the past
criteria.then: no STALE problem is produced and every otherwise valid request is accepted: the no-arg constructor performs no staleness check at all, so existing behaviour (including SampleBatchTest's 13 → 10 → 6 counts for the unchanged sample-batch.json) is untouched

criteria.given: the new validator constructor
criteria.when: called as new WorkRequestValidator(null, Duration.ofDays(30)), new WorkRequestValidator(Clock.systemUTC(), null) or new WorkRequestValidator(Clock.systemUTC(), Duration.ofHours(12))
criteria.then: the first two throw NullPointerException (messages "clock" and "maxAge") and the third throws IllegalArgumentException because maxAge must be at least one day

criteria.given: a validator with a fixed clock and 30 day max age
criteria.when: validate is called with two requests whose requestedAt are both exactly 30 days and 1 second before that clock instant
criteria.then: both are reported STALE; the clock is read once per validate call (a single clock.instant()) so every request in a batch is compared against the same now

criteria.given: a WorkRequestProcessor built with a staleness-aware validator (fixed clock, 30 days), the real DuplicateResolver and WorkRequestSorter
criteria.when: process runs on a batch where R-1 (recent, MEDIUM) and R-2 (90 days old, CRITICAL) have the same equipmentId and the same normalized description
criteria.then: the result problems contain exactly one problem for R-2 with code STALE and no DUPLICATE problem, R-1 stays in the queue with priority MEDIUM (no escalation from the stale request), and the trace still has exactly three entries validate/deduplicate/prioritize with validate out == deduplicate in: stale requests are removed before deduplication and never influence later stages

criteria.given: a batch containing stale requests, invalid requests and duplicates
criteria.when: the same batch is processed 100 times in shuffled order through a staleness-aware processor with a fixed clock
criteria.then: the accepted queue, the problem list and the trace notes are identical every time; within the validate stage problems are ordered by input index with stale and field problems interleaved in that single index order, and all validate-stage problems precede deduplicate-stage problems

criteria.given: a new @ConfigurationProperties("app.staleness") record StalenessProperties(@DefaultValue("30d") Duration maxAge)
criteria.when: the context starts with no app.staleness.* property set, then with app.staleness.max-age=7d, then with app.staleness.max-age=0d
criteria.then: maxAge binds to Duration.ofDays(30), then Duration.ofDays(7), and 0d (or any value under one day, or a negative value) fails startup because the record constructor throws IllegalArgumentException containing "app.staleness.max-age must be at least 1 day"; src/main/resources/application.yml states the 30d default explicitly under app.staleness.max-age

criteria.given: the Spring context (ProcessingConfig)
criteria.when: it is started
criteria.then: it contains exactly one java.time.Clock bean named "clock" whose default value is Clock.systemUTC() and which a test configuration can replace with Clock.fixed(...), and the WorkRequestValidator bean is created with that Clock and StalenessProperties.maxAge, so the wired pipeline does flag stale requests; the existing no-arg and multi-arg constructors of WorkRequestValidator, DuplicateResolver, WorkRequestSorter and WorkRequestProcessor remain usable unchanged

criteria.given: the running API with a Clock fixed at 2026-10-20T12:00:00Z and the default 30 day max age
criteria.when: a batch containing a request requestedAt 2026-08-01T08:00:00Z is posted, and separately the unchanged 13-request sample batch (all requestedAt 2026-10-20) is processed
criteria.then: the response for the first batch contains a ProblemDto with code "STALE", field "requestedAt" and the stale message, and the request is absent from the returned queue; the sample batch produces no STALE problem and keeps its pinned queue, problems and 13 → 10 → 6 trace counts

criteria.given: BatchObserver and its metrics registration
criteria.when: a batch containing a stale request is observed
criteria.then: a counter exists for STALE following the same naming scheme as the other ProblemCode counters and is incremented once per stale problem; counters are derived from ProblemCode.values() so the set stays one counter per code (now six)

outOfScope: Adding a fourth pipeline stage or a fourth StageTrace entry for staleness (the check lives inside the existing validate stage)
Keeping stale requests in the queue with a 'stale' marker on WorkRequest or WorkRequestDto
Adding stale rows to src/main/resources/sample-batch.json or changing its pinned 13 → 10 → 6 expectations
A new ProblemCode or problem for future-dated requestedAt (clock skew)
Per-priority or per-equipment max ages, and sub-day max age durations
A request parameter, header or endpoint that overrides the max age per call
Changing sort order, duplicate resolution or validation rules for non-stale requests
Notifications, archiving, or persistence of stale requests, and any frontend/UI change
Replacing other Instant.now() usages elsewhere in the codebase with the new Clock bean
data.title: Flag requests older than 30 days as STALE and keep them out of the queue

criteria.then: the result problems contain exactly one problem for R-2 with code STALE and no DUPLICATE problem, R-1 stays in the queue with priority MEDIUM (no escalation from the stale request), and the trace still has exactly three entries validate/deduplicate/prioritize with validate out == deduplicate in: stale requests are removed before deduplication and never influence later stages

criteria.given: a batch containing stale requests, invalid requests and duplicates
criteria.when: the same batch is processed 100 times in shuffled order through a staleness-aware processor with a fixed clock
criteria.then: the accepted queue, the problem list and the trace notes are identical every time; within the validate stage problems are ordered by input index with stale and field problems interleaved in that single index order, and all validate-stage problems precede deduplicate-stage problems

criteria.given: a new @ConfigurationProperties("app.staleness") record StalenessProperties(@DefaultValue("30d") Duration maxAge)
criteria.when: the context starts with no app.staleness.* property set, then with app.staleness.max-age=7d, then with app.staleness.max-age=0d
criteria.then: maxAge binds to Duration.ofDays(30), then Duration.ofDays(7), and 0d (or any value under one day, or a negative value) fails startup because the record constructor throws IllegalArgumentException containing "app.staleness.max-age must be at least 1 day"; src/main/resources/application.yml states the 30d default explicitly under app.staleness.max-age

criteria.given: the Spring context (ProcessingConfig)
criteria.when: it is started
criteria.then: it contains exactly one java.time.Clock bean named "clock" whose default value is Clock.systemUTC() and which a test configuration can replace with Clock.fixed(...), and the WorkRequestValidator bean is created with that Clock and StalenessProperties.maxAge, so the wired pipeline does flag stale requests; the existing no-arg and multi-arg constructors of WorkRequestValidator, DuplicateResolver, WorkRequestSorter and WorkRequestProcessor remain usable unchanged

criteria.given: the running API with a Clock fixed at 2026-10-20T12:00:00Z and the default 30 day max age
criteria.when: a batch containing a request requestedAt 2026-08-01T08:00:00Z is posted, and separately the unchanged 13-request sample batch (all requestedAt 2026-10-20) is processed
criteria.then: the response for the first batch contains a ProblemDto with code "STALE", field "requestedAt" and the stale message, and the request is absent from the returned queue; the sample batch produces no STALE problem and keeps its pinned queue, problems and 13 → 10 → 6 trace counts

criteria.given: BatchObserver and its metrics registration
criteria.when: a batch containing a stale request is observed
criteria.then: a counter exists for STALE following the same naming scheme as the other ProblemCode counters and is incremented once per stale problem; counters are derived from ProblemCode.values() so the set stays one counter per code (now six)

outOfScope: Adding a fourth pipeline stage or a fourth StageTrace entry for staleness (the check lives inside the existing validate stage)
Keeping stale requests in the queue with a 'stale' marker on WorkRequest or WorkRequestDto
Adding stale rows to src/main/resources/sample-batch.json or changing its pinned 13 → 10 → 6 expectations
A new ProblemCode or problem for future-dated requestedAt (clock skew)
Per-priority or per-equipment max ages, and sub-day max age durations
A request parameter, header or endpoint that overrides the max age per call
Changing sort order, duplicate resolution or validation rules for non-stale requests
Notifications, archiving, or persistence of stale requests, and any frontend/UI change
Replacing other Instant.now() usages elsewhere in the codebase with the new Clock bean
structured_output.title: Flag requests older than 30 days as STALE and keep them out of the queue
